# v0.26.2-rc2 — long user messages reach the agent (#1016)

**RELEASE CANDIDATE — not GA.** This prerelease replaces `v0.26.2-rc1` and enters the RELEASE-READINESS-V1 gauntlet
(bench/specs/RELEASE-READINESS-V1.md) at this tag, in full:
- **Phase A:** the all-tools live matrix on a fresh clone across privacy postures, plus the planted-secret battery,
  bound to `hermes-lcm-x v0.26.2 (15 tools)`.
- **Phase B, P0/P1 adversarial sweep** of the full `v0.26.1`→rc2 diff: correctness, security/privacy, performance/DoS,
  API contract, upgrade/migration (mandatory: a `v0.26.1`-created store, including its placeholder rows, opened under
  this tree) and concurrency; independent finders with 2-vote verification, across model families.
- **Phase B, hands-on lane:** the release's own fault cell, the seam check, on a real host at this tag with the
  reference agent's externalization settings (a ~15,000-character paste stays full text in the host transcript and in
  the LCM store; a ~150,000-character paste becomes a stub with a preview and a read hint; tool output is unchanged
  from `v0.26.1`), plus the regression suites on each supported host build at this tag.
- **Phase C:** the host cells (a live `hermes acp` soak with at least one committed compaction).
- **Recall scorecard, fast tier (#898):** embeddings off, at this tag against `v0.26.1`, question by question.

This is a patch on a minor that already passed its 24-hour reference-agent window, so no new window runs (the window
is a per-minor gate). GA follows only when the receipts are green. The GA tree is this tree plus the `v0.26.2`
release-notes file.

**GA accepts when:**
- **Gauntlet.** Phase A, B and C receipts are green at this tag.
- **The fix holds on a real host.** The seam check passes: the short paste is full text, the long paste is a stub with
  a preview and a read hint, and tool output matches `v0.26.1`.
- **Recall.** 0 per-question `lcm_recall` flips against `v0.26.1` on the fast tier.
- **Defects.** No respin-bar defect that managed profiles can reach is open: a loss, a duplicate row or reset that
  `v0.26.1` does not show, a wedge, or an over-window request.

Patch release on top of `v0.26.1` (`5fc3d1c6`), cut from `release/v0.26.x`. Theme: what a person pastes, the agent
reads.
- **Before:** with large-output externalization on, a user or assistant message longer than the externalization
  threshold (12,000 characters in the reference agent's configuration) was stored as a one-line stub with no preview
  and no read hint. For a user message the stub also replaced the paste in what the model received, from the turn the
  paste arrived onward, so the agent never saw it and was not told how to open it. Assistant text stayed in the live
  conversation, but for both roles full-text search and recall could not find the words.
- **After:** user, assistant and other non-tool message text below 100,000 characters and below about 25,000
  estimated tokens (dense scripts such as CJK reach that count sooner) is never externalized; it is stored and
  replayed as written. Above either bound the stub carries a short preview of the start and end of the text and a read
  hint (`read it with lcm_expand`), so the agent can open the full text on demand.
- **Unchanged:** tool output and media follow the existing externalization rules and threshold. No config key was
  added, removed or renamed.
- **Already-stored stubs** are not rewritten. Each one is still readable with `lcm_expand`.
- No tool name or count changed (15 tools); `LCM plugin loaded` and every `lcm_*` name are unchanged.
- No new setting, no prompt change beyond one clause of the system note (below), no schema change (schema 5) and no
  new table.
- This release never moves a deployed pin by itself. A deployment moves only when its operator re-pins it.

## Changes since v0.26.2-rc1

The rc1 Phase B sweep confirmed two defects in the new stub preview, each by two independent verifiers. Both are
fixed here (#1031), so the whole gauntlet runs again at this tag.
- **P0, replay identity (upgrade/migration dimension).** When the head or tail of a message over the floor contained the
  text `quarantined_assistant_output`, the preview copied it into the stub. The replay identity matcher skips a stub
  that holds that text, so each cold restart appended the session's history again (5 rows became 10, 19 and 30 across
  restarts in the repro). `v0.26.1` reading the same store after a rollback did the same. The preview now writes the
  token as `quarantined-assistant-output`, in any case.
- **P1, credential in the preview (security/privacy dimension).** The tail scan could begin inside a credential and keep
  its value without its label (for example `ey='<key>'` from `api_key='<key>'`). The embedding privacy step then no
  longer recognized the value, so a cloud embedding provider with chunk backfill on could receive it. Each scan window
  now passes through the plugin's existing sensitive-text patterns (`private_key` first, then `api_key`,
  `bearer_token`, `password_assignment`) before it is collapsed and sliced, whatever the redaction setting. The tail
  scan also starts up to 8,192 characters before its window, so it sees the label, or the PEM BEGIN line, of a
  credential the window cuts. It drops a run of credential characters that its own start cuts, so even a longer
  credential leaves no unlabeled tail. No
  pattern was added. The stored original, tool output and media are unchanged. Known limits (#1034): a quoted password
  with no closing quote, or a PEM body pasted without its BEGIN/END lines, is not recognised in previews or in inline
  text; and a credential more than about 8,000 characters from its label, or a quoted multi-word secret longer than
  the scan, can still leave a fragment in the preview.
- **Tests (#1031):** 15 test cases fail at `v0.26.2-rc1` and pass here:
  - a key whose label the tail scan cut off (two label forms);
  - the chunk privacy preparation leaving no key fragment;
  - a cold replay of the same history to a fresh engine on the same store adding no row, with the quarantine token in
    the preview (both roles, two cases);
  - the adversarial-preview test, extended with the token (three positions);
  - from the reviews of #1031: a label just outside the tail window (adjacent and spaced forms), credentials of 5,000
    and 12,000 characters ending the paste, and a truncated PEM key (a BEGIN line and 50 body lines) ending the paste.

  Three controls pass at both trees: a key whose label sits in the head, an ordinary preview that stays
  byte-identical, and unbroken CJK text that keeps its tail. One existing test expected the tail to show the end of a
  200,000-character run of one letter; that run is now dropped, and the test was updated.
- **Upgrading from rc1.** rc2 fixes the stubs it writes; it does not rewrite stubs that `v0.26.2-rc1` already wrote.
  rc1 was a prerelease for about a day, and no managed deployment pinned it; none of the 16 stores its gauntlet wrote
  holds an affected stub. A store that did run rc1 can still hold a stub whose preview quotes
  `quarantined_assistant_output` (the cold-replay duplication above) or ends in a credential fragment, which is sent on
  only when cloud embeddings and chunk backfill are on. For such a store, restore the affected sessions from a backup
  taken before rc1, and keep cloud embeddings off until that is done.
- The sweep's two P3 findings are follow-ups, not respin defects: #1032 (a repeat protection of a 12k–100k message that
  holds a long base64 run writes another payload file) and #1033 (`lcm_grep` with the non-default
  `content_scope="both"` returns a long paste twice).

## Changes since v0.26.1

- **#1016 (#1020): user, assistant and other non-tool text is externalized only above 100,000 characters or about
  25,000 estimated tokens, whichever comes first.**
  - Below both bounds that text is never externalized, whatever the configured threshold. Both bounds are code
    constants, not settings.
  - Above them the stub keeps its prefix and keeps `ref=` as the last field, and adds a whitespace-collapsed head and
    tail preview and the read hint `lcm_expand(externalized_ref=…)`. The preview is built from bounded scans of the
    text's two ends, so a very large message is never copied whole to build it, and it is sanitized so message text
    cannot end the stub or forge a ref.
  - The whole stub stays within the existing 512-character placeholder bound, so `v0.26.1` and older readers still
    recognize it after a rollback.
  - The system note now names these stubs as readable with `lcm_expand` (one clause).
  - Tool output, media payloads and the externalization settings are unchanged.
- **Tests (#1020):** a new regression file covers a 15,000-character user and assistant turn (stored inline, found by
  full-text search and recall, carried to the model), a 150,000-character turn (stub with preview and read hint,
  expandable to the original), an unchanged tool-output stub, a rollback reader frozen from `v0.26.1`, and adversarial
  text that tries to forge or end the stub. The new file was red on `v0.26.1`'s code before the fix. Existing tests
  whose subject is an externalized user or assistant row now use payloads above the floor or lift the floor
  explicitly; no assertion was removed or weakened.
- **Docs:** this patch's identity.

## Qualification

- **Cross-model review.** #1020 was reviewed across models before merge. Its merge-blocking finding, a stub that
  could exceed the 512-character bound older readers enforce, was fixed before merge, with rollback-reader tests that
  fail without the fix. #1031 was written on the Claude side and reviewed by Codex and by a separate Claude reviewer
  before merge. Two review bots, the Claude reviewer and a second Codex pass found the tail-window boundary cases (a label
  or a PEM BEGIN line just outside the window), which are fixed in the same PR. Codex raised one more concern: stubs that rc1 wrote keep the token. It does not apply, because rc1 is a
  prerelease that no deployment pins; none of the 16 stores the rc1 gauntlet wrote holds such a stub.
- **Phase B at rc1.** Six dimension finders (correctness, security/privacy, performance/DoS, API contract,
  upgrade/migration, concurrency) found P0 1, P1 1 and P3 2, and nothing in correctness or performance/DoS. Codex ran
  four of the finders and Claude ran two. Two independent Claude verifiers confirmed both the P0 and the P1, each with
  a reproduction; the Codex verifiers were refused by the provider's safety filter. Both defects are fixed above.
- **Full suite** at this tree, run the CI way: 6,248 passed, 92 skipped, 16 xfailed, 0 failed.
- The gauntlet runs AT THE `v0.26.2-rc2` TAG (the phases at the top, on `v0.26.1..v0.26.2-rc2`), and its receipts are
  what the GA notes link.

## Known follow-ups

- From the rc1 sweep: #1032 and #1033 (both P3). From the review of #1031: #1034 (P3).

## Benchmark boundary

- No retrieval or QA benchmark claim. The change is confined to which messages are externalized and to the shape of
  the stub above the floor.
- The recall scorecard's fast tier (#898: embeddings off, every rc) runs at this tag against `v0.26.1`, question by
  question. Its bar is 0 per-question `lcm_recall` flips. The embeddings-on rows are per-minor and do not run for this
  patch.

## Upgrade

- **Install:** plugin only. Verify the exact commit, install this tag at it and restart the gateway. No migration.
- **Rollback:** to `v0.26.1`, plugin only. The store is unchanged (schema 5); text stored in full by this version is
  ordinary text to `v0.26.1`, and stubs it writes stay readable there.
- **Settings:** none.
